text:
*PSY516 GDB  Solution*

Both of the given statements are myths and logically false.

It is wrong to say that statistics lie. Statistics is an objective and evidence-based discipline. It is a tool, and like any tool, its result depends on the user. If a researcher uses faulty sampling, manipulates data, or makes a biased interpretation, then the conclusion will be wrong. But that is the fault of the person, not statistics. In reality, statistics protects us from lies by giving us proper tests and rules.

Similarly, the concept that non-significant results have no value is a misunderstanding. A result with p > .05 does not mean the study is meaningless. It just means the alternative hypothesis was not supported by the data. That information is still a scientific contribution.

*Importance of Null Findings:*
Null findings are very important in psychology because they reduce publication bias. If we only publish significant results, our literature becomes one-sided.

*Example:* For instance, a study is done to test if online motivational quotes increase self-esteem. The results come out non-significant. This null finding is helpful because it tells counselors that just reading quotes is not enough to improve self-esteem and more structured therapy is needed.

*Negative impact on students:* These myths create stats phobia. Students start thinking statistics is fake and only significant results are real research. This narrow thinking stops them from learning the true spirit of research where every systematic finding, whether significant or not, adds to knowledge.
